info.description:
# IdentityForge API

IdentityForge is a production-ready Authentication and Authorization backend built using Node.js, Express.js and TypeScript.

It provides secure authentication, authorization, session management and user management APIs designed for scalable production applications.

---

## Features

- User Registration
    
- Email Verification
    
- Secure Login
    
- JWT Authentication
    
- HttpOnly Cookie Authentication
    
- Refresh Token Rotation
    
- Password Reset
    
- Password Change
    
- Session Management
    
- Role Based Access Control (RBAC)
    
- Admin APIs
    
- Redis Caching
    
- Background Email Queue (BullMQ)
    

---

## Base URL

{{baseUrl}}

Example

[http://localhost:5000/api/v1](http://localhost:5000/api/v1)

---

## Authentication

IdentityForge uses Cookie Based Authentication.

After successful login the server sends

- if_accessToken
    
- if_refreshToken
    

Both cookies are:

- HttpOnly
    
- SameSite=Strict
    
- Secure in Production
    

Postman automatically stores these cookies.

No Authorization header is required for authenticated requests.

---

## Response Format

Every API returns a consistent response.

Example

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Request successful.",
    "data": {}
}

 ```

---

## Error Format

``` json
{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Validation failed.",
    "errors": []
}

 ```

---

## Status Codes

200 OK

201 Created

400 Bad Request

401 Unauthorized

403 Forbidden

404 Not Found

409 Conflict

500 Internal Server Error

---

## API Modules

Authentication

User

Admin

System

---

## Technologies

Node.js

Express.js

TypeScript

Prisma ORM

PostgreSQL

Redis

BullMQ

JWT

Zod Validation

Winston Logger

Docker

request.description:
# Signup

Creates a new user account.

A verification email is automatically sent after successful registration.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/signup

---

## Authentication

Not Required

---

## Request Body

``` json
{
    "firstName":"Harshit",
    "lastName":"Kumar",
    "email":"harshit@example.com",
    "password":"Harshit@123"
}

 ```

---

## Success Response

201 Created

``` json
{
    "success":true,
    "message":"Account created successfully. Please verify your email.",
    "data":{}
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

400 Validation Error

409 Email Already Exists

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Password is securely hashed.

A verification token is generated.

Verification email is queued using BullMQ.

User cannot login until email verification is completed.

# Login

Authenticates an existing user.

Creates a new authenticated session.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/login

---

## Authentication

Not Required

---

## Request Body

``` json
{
    "email":"harshit@example.com",
    "password":"Harshit@123"
}

 ```

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success":true,
    "message":"Login successful.",
    "data":{
        "id":"...",
        "email":"...",
        "firstName":"...",
        "lastName":"...",
        "username":"...",
        "role":"USER"
    }
}

 ```

---

## Cookies

if_accessToken

if_refreshToken

Automatically stored by Postman.

---

## Possible Errors

401 Invalid Credentials

403 Account Locked

403 Deleted Account

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Creates a new session.

Stores refresh token inside database.

Resets failed login attempts.

Updates last login timestamp.

Returns authenticated user information.

# Logout

Logs out the currently authenticated user.

Removes the current authenticated session and clears authentication cookies.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/logout

---

## Authentication

Required

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success":true,
    "message":"Logout successful."
}

 ```

---

## Cookies Cleared

if_accessToken

if_refreshToken

---

## Notes

Deletes refresh token from database.

Deletes active session.

Clears Redis cache.

Logout is always successful even if cookies are already expired.

# Refresh Access Token

Generates a new Access Token and Refresh Token using the existing Refresh Token.

Implements Refresh Token Rotation.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/refresh-token

---

## Authentication

Refresh Token Cookie Required

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success":true,
    "message":"Token refreshed successfully.",
    "data":{}
}

 ```

---

## Cookies Updated

if_accessToken

if_refreshToken

---

## Possible Errors

401 Refresh Token Missing

401 Refresh Token Invalid

401 Refresh Token Expired

404 User Not Found

---

## Notes

Old Refresh Token is deleted.

New Refresh Token is created.

Session activity timestamp is updated.

New HttpOnly cookies are sent.

# Verify Email

Verifies a user's email address using a verification token.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/verify-email

---

## Authentication

Not Required

---

token

Example

Deletes verification token after successful verification.

# Resend Verification Email

Generates a new email verification token and sends a new verification email.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/resend-verification

---

## Authentication

Required

---

Queues a new verification email.

request.description:
# Forgot Password

Generates a secure password reset token and sends a password reset email to the user.

For security reasons, this endpoint always returns a success response, even if the email address does not exist.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/forgot-password

---

## Authentication

Not Required

---

## Request Body

``` json
{
    "email": "harshit@example.com"
}

 ```

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "If an account with this email exists, a password reset link has been sent."
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

400 Validation Error

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Security

This endpoint prevents user enumeration.

Whether the email exists or not, the API returns the same success response.

Attackers cannot determine whether an account exists.

---

## Notes

Any previous unused password reset tokens are deleted.

A new secure password reset token is generated.

Only the hashed token is stored in the database.

A password reset email is queued using BullMQ.

# Reset Password

Resets a user's password using a valid password reset token.

All active sessions are revoked after a successful password reset.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/reset-password

---

## Authentication

Not Required

---

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| token | Yes | Password reset token |

Example

POST /auth/reset-password?token=xxxxxxxx

---

## Request Body

``` json
{
    "newPassword": "NewPassword@123"
}

 ```

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Password has been reset successfully."
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

400 Invalid Token

400 Token Already Used

400 Token Expired

400 New Password Matches Current Password

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Security

Password reset tokens are one-time use.

Only hashed reset tokens are stored in the database.

---

## Notes

Updates the user's password.

Marks the reset token as used.

Deletes all refresh tokens.

Deletes all user sessions.

Clears Redis cached profile.

Clears authentication cookies.

# Change Password

Allows an authenticated user to change their password.

Changing the password automatically logs the user out from every device.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/change-password

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Request Body

``` json
{
    "currentPassword": "CurrentPassword@123",
    "newPassword": "NewPassword@123"
}

 ```

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Password changed successfully."
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

400 Current Password Incorrect

400 New Password Matches Current Password

401 Unauthorized

404 User Not Found

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Verifies the current password.

Hashes the new password.

Deletes every refresh token.

Deletes every active session.

Clears Redis cached profile.

Clears authentication cookies.

The user must login again after changing the password.

# Get Current User

Returns the currently authenticated user's profile.

This endpoint uses Redis caching to improve response time.

---

## Endpoint

GET /auth/me

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Profile fetched successfully.",
    "data": {
        "user": {
            "id": "...",
            "firstName": "...",
            "lastName": "...",
            "username": "...",
            "email": "...",
            "role": "USER",
            "isEmailVerified": true,
            "createdAt": "...",
            "updatedAt": "...",
            "lastLoginAt": "..."
        }
    },
    "cached": false
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

401 Unauthorized

404 User Not Found

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Cache

The response includes

``` json
{
    "cached": true
}

 ```

when served from Redis.

Otherwise

``` json
{
    "cached": false
}

 ```

The profile is cached for five minutes.

---

## Notes

Checks Redis before querying the database.

Stores user profile in Redis after a cache miss.

Returns only public profile information.

# Revoke All Sessions

Logs the user out from every device by deleting all active sessions and refresh tokens.

The current session is also revoked.

---

## Endpoint

POST /auth/revoke-all-sessions

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "All sessions revoked successfully."
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

401 Unauthorized

404 User Not Found

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Deletes every refresh token associated with the user.

Deletes every active session.

Clears Redis cached profile.

Clears authentication cookies.

The user must login again on every device.

item.description:
# Authentication APIs

Authentication APIs manage user identity, authentication and account security.

These endpoints allow users to:

- Create an account
    
- Verify email
    
- Login
    
- Logout
    
- Refresh authentication
    
- Reset password
    
- Change password
    
- Manage sessions
    

---

## Authentication Strategy

Cookie Based Authentication

The backend stores authentication tokens inside secure HttpOnly cookies.

Clients never receive JWT tokens directly.

---

## Security Features

Password Hashing

Email Verification

Refresh Token Rotation

Session Tracking

Account Locking

Password Reset Tokens

Redis Caching

Secure Cookies

---

## Available APIs

POST /auth/signup

POST /auth/login

POST /auth/logout

POST /auth/refresh-token

POST /auth/verify-email

POST /auth/resend-verification

POST /auth/forgot-password

POST /auth/reset-password

POST /auth/change-password

GET /auth/me

POST /auth/revoke-all-sessions

---

## Authentication Flow

User Signup

↓

Verification Email Sent

↓

Verify Email

↓

Login

↓

HttpOnly Cookies Created

↓

Authenticated Requests

↓

Refresh Token Rotation

↓

Logout

or

↓

Revoke All Sessions

---

## Password Recovery Flow

Forgot Password

↓

Password Reset Email

↓

Reset Password

↓

Logout From Every Device

↓

Login Again

request.description:
# Update Profile

Updates the authenticated user's profile information.

Only the fields provided in the request body are updated.

---

## Endpoint

PATCH /users/profile

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Request Body

``` json
{
    "firstName": "Harshit",
    "lastName": "Kumar",
    "username": "harshitdev"
}

 ```

All fields are optional.

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Profile updated successfully.",
    "data": {
        "id": "...",
        "firstName": "...",
        "lastName": "...",
        "username": "...",
        "email": "...",
        "avatarUrl": null,
        "role": "USER",
        "status": "ACTIVE",
        "isEmailVerified": true,
        "updatedAt": "..."
    }
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

400 Validation Error

401 Unauthorized

404 User Not Found

409 Username Already Taken

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Only supplied fields are updated.

Username must be unique.

Redis cached profile is automatically invalidated.

Email cannot be updated using this endpoint.

# Delete Account

Soft deletes the authenticated user's account.

The account is marked as deleted instead of being permanently removed from the database.

---

## Endpoint

DELETE /users/account

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Account deleted successfully."
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

401 Unauthorized

404 User Not Found

400 Account Already Deleted

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Performs a soft delete.

User status becomes DELETED.

Deletes all refresh tokens.

Deletes all active sessions.

Clears Redis cached profile.

Clears authentication cookies.

The user is logged out from every device immediately.

request.description:
# Get Active Sessions

Returns all active sessions associated with the authenticated user.

Expired sessions are automatically excluded.

---

## Endpoint

GET /users/sessions

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Sessions fetched successfully.",
    "data": {
        "sessions": [
            {
                "id": "...",
                "ipAddress": "...",
                "browser": "...",
                "os": "...",
                "device": "...",
                "country": "...",
                "city": "...",
                "isCurrent": true,
                "lastUsedAt": "...",
                "expiresAt": "...",
                "createdAt": "..."
            }
        ],
        "total": 1
    }
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

401 Unauthorized

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Only active sessions are returned.

Sessions are sorted by most recently used.

The current session is identified using the `isCurrent` property.

Useful for account security dashboards.

# Revoke Session

Terminates a specific session belonging to the authenticated user.

This endpoint allows users to logout from individual devices without affecting the current session.

---

## Endpoint

DELETE /users/sessions/:sessionId

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Path Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sessionId | Session identifier |

Example

DELETE /users/sessions/cmrah4ttq0000zwlamscdmjwm

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Session revoked successfully."
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

401 Unauthorized

403 Forbidden

404 Session Not Found

400 Current Session Cannot Be Revoked

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Security

Users cannot revoke sessions belonging to another user.

The current session cannot be revoked individually.

---

## Notes

Deletes the selected session.

Associated refresh tokens are automatically removed through database cascade rules.

Other active sessions remain unaffected.

To logout from every device, use the **Revoke All Sessions** endpoint instead.

item.description:
# User APIs

User APIs allow authenticated users to manage their own account.

These endpoints provide profile management, account deletion and session management.

---

## Authentication

All endpoints in this module require authentication.

Authentication is performed using HttpOnly Cookies.

---

## Features

- Update Profile
    
- Delete Account
    
- View Active Sessions
    
- Revoke Individual Sessions
    

---

## Security

• Only authenticated users can access these endpoints.

• Users can only access their own resources.

• Session revocation prevents users from revoking sessions belonging to other users.

• Current session cannot be revoked individually.

---

## Cache

User profile updates automatically invalidate cached profile data stored in Redis.

---

## Available APIs

PATCH /users/profile

DELETE /users/account

GET /users/sessions

DELETE /users/sessions/:sessionId

---

## User Management Flow

Login

↓

View Profile

↓

Update Profile

↓

View Active Sessions

↓

Revoke Old Device Sessions

↓

Delete Account (Optional)

---

## Session Management

Current Device

✓ Cannot Be Revoked Individually

Other Devices

✓ Can Be Revoked

All Devices

✓ Use Revoke All Sessions API

---

## Cache Behaviour

Get Current User

↓

Redis Cache

↓

Profile Updated

↓

Cache Invalidated

↓

Next Request Fetches Fresh Data

request.description:
# Get All Users

Returns a paginated list of users.

Results are cached using Redis to improve performance.

---

## Endpoint

GET /admin/users

---

## Authentication

Required

Administrator Access

---

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| page | No | Page number (Default: 1) |
| limit | No | Number of users per page (Default: 10, Maximum: 100) |

Example

GET /admin/users?page=1&limit=10

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Users fetched successfully.",
    "data": {
        "users": [],
        "pagination": {
            "page": 1,
            "limit": 10,
            "totalUsers": 100,
            "totalPages": 10,
            "hasNextPage": true,
            "hasPreviousPage": false
        }
    },
    "cached": false
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

401 Unauthorized

403 Forbidden

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Cache

Responses are cached for five minutes.

The response includes

``` json
{
    "cached": true
}

 ```

when served from Redis.

---

## Notes

Users are sorted by newest accounts first.

Pagination metadata is included.

Redis cache is automatically invalidated whenever a user is updated or deleted.

# Get User By ID

Returns detailed information for a specific user.

---

## Endpoint

GET /admin/users/:id

---

## Authentication

Required

Administrator Access

---

## Path Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| id | User Identifier |

Example

GET /admin/users/cmrddevje0000tkla718m2w4q

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "User fetched successfully.",
    "data": {
        "id": "...",
        "firstName": "...",
        "lastName": "...",
        "email": "...",
        "role": "USER",
        "status": "ACTIVE",
        "isEmailVerified": true,
        "createdAt": "...",
        "updatedAt": "..."
    },
    "cached": false
}

 ```

---

## Possible Errors

401 Unauthorized

403 Forbidden

404 User Not Found

500 Internal Server Error

---

## Notes

Checks Redis before querying the database.

Stores the user in Redis after a cache miss.

Returns only administrative user information.

item.description:
# Admin APIs

Admin APIs provide administrative access to manage users within the IdentityForge platform.

These endpoints allow administrators to view users, inspect user details, update user roles, manage account status and perform administrative actions.

---

## Authentication

Required

HttpOnly Authentication Cookies

---

## Authorization

Administrator Only

Users without administrative privileges are not allowed to access these endpoints.

---

## Features

- List Users
    
- View User Details
    
- Update User Role
    
- Update User Status
    
- Delete User
    

---

## Cache

User list and user detail responses are cached using Redis.

Whenever a user is updated or deleted, the related cache entries are automatically invalidated.

---

## Available APIs

GET /admin/users

GET /admin/users/:id

PATCH /admin/users/:id/role

PATCH /admin/users/:id/status

DELETE /admin/users/:id

---

## Administrative Workflow

Administrator Login

↓

View Users

↓

Inspect User Details

↓

Update User Role

↓

Update User Status

↓

Delete User (If Required)

---

## Cache Behaviour

Get Users

↓

Redis Cache

↓

Update User

↓

Invalidate User Cache

↓

Invalidate Paginated User Cache

↓

Next Request Fetches Fresh Data

---

## Security

Only authenticated administrators can access these endpoints.

Administrative actions immediately invalidate cached user data to ensure consistency across the application.

Deleted users are soft deleted by updating their account status rather than removing records from the database.

request.description:
# Health Check

Returns the overall health status of the application.

This endpoint verifies that all critical dependencies required by the application are functioning correctly.

---

## Endpoint

GET /system/health

---

## Authentication

Not Required

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Application is healthy.",
    "data": {
        "status": "healthy",
        "services": {
            "database": "up",
            "redis": "up"
        }
    }
}

 ```

---

## Failure Response

503 Service Unavailable

``` json
{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Application is unhealthy.",
    "data": {
        "status": "unhealthy",
        "services": {
            "database": "down",
            "redis": "up"
        }
    }
}

 ```

---

## Notes

Checks database connectivity.

Checks Redis connectivity.

Returns HTTP 503 if any required dependency is unavailable.

Used by monitoring systems to determine application health.

# Readiness Check

Determines whether the application is ready to receive incoming requests.

Unlike the liveness endpoint, readiness verifies that required services are available before traffic is routed to the application.

---

## Endpoint

GET /system/ready

---

## Authentication

Not Required

---

## Success Response

200 OK

``` json
{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Application is ready.",
    "data": {
        "ready": true,
        "services": {
            "database": "up",
            "redis": "up"
        }
    }
}

 ```

---

## Failure Response

503 Service Unavailable

``` json
{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Application is not ready.",
    "data": {
        "ready": false,
        "services": {
            "database": "down",
            "redis": "up"
        }
    }
}

 ```

---

## Notes

Used by Kubernetes readiness probes.

Ensures traffic is only routed to healthy instances.

Requires both the database and Redis to be available.

Determines whether the application process is currently running.

This endpoint confirms that the server process is alive.

---

Not Required

## Notes

Does not verify database or Redis connectivity.

Commonly used by Kubernetes liveness probes.

If this endpoint fails, the application instance should be restarted.

item.description:
# System APIs

System APIs provide operational and monitoring information about the IdentityForge application.

These endpoints are intended for infrastructure, monitoring tools, deployment pipelines and administrators.

---

## Authentication

Not Required

All endpoints are publicly accessible.

---

## Features

- Health Monitoring
    
- Readiness Checks
    
- Liveness Checks
    
- Application Version
    
- Application Information
    

---

## Typical Consumers

- Docker
    
- Kubernetes
    
- Nginx
    
- Prometheus
    
- Grafana
    
- Uptime Monitoring Services
    
- CI/CD Pipelines
    
- DevOps Engineers
    

---

## Available APIs

GET /system/health

GET /system/ready

GET /system/live

GET /system/version

GET /system/info

---

## System Monitoring Flow

Application Starts

↓

Health Check

↓

Readiness Check

↓

Receive Traffic

↓

Liveness Monitoring

↓

Version Verification

↓

Application Information

---

## Health Monitoring

Health

↓

Checks Database

↓

Checks Redis

↓

Returns Overall Application Health

---

## Infrastructure Usage

Health Endpoint

Used by monitoring systems.

Ready Endpoint

Used by load balancers and Kubernetes.

Live Endpoint

Used to determine if the application process should be restarted.

Version Endpoint

Used to verify deployed releases.

Info Endpoint

Used for diagnostics and operational visibility.
